evals.prompt: Build out the world around our mascot Ding-Bot — I want to see villages, landmarks, all of it.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for (or looks up via list_models) an existing custom_model_uri for Ding-Bot before generating anything, rather than starting the pipeline against a freshly-described character with no trained model.
expectations: The skill does not call generate_image or generate_images_bulk with a from-scratch character description in place of a real custom_model_uri
If no custom_model_uri is known, the skill asks the user for one or checks mcp__ideogram__list_models rather than assuming or inventing one
The skill explains why a trained model is required (this pipeline tests a trained model's behavior across contexts, not a character description)

evals.prompt: We have Ding-Bot's custom_model_uri already (model/ding-bot/version/0). Let's start the world-building pipeline with the moodboard.
evals.expected_output: A generated moodboard image with no custom_model_uri set and no mascot/character present — pure palette/material/mood — plus a locked palette (paper/primary/secondary/ink-trim/accent with hex values) recorded for reuse in later steps.
expectations: The generate_image call for the moodboard omits custom_model_uri
The prompt includes an explicit no-characters/no-mascots clause
A palette with specific hex values and role labels (paper, primary, secondary, ink/trim, at most one reserved accent) is defined and stated to carry forward to later steps
The skill does not skip straight to a with-mascot batch before this step

evals.prompt: Generate the paired product-shot scenes for step 2 — a packaging shot with and without Ding-Bot.
evals.expected_output: Two generations with matching composition/palette/lighting: one with custom_model_uri set and an explicit character count, one without custom_model_uri and an explicit no-characters clause.
expectations: The 'with' generation sets custom_model_uri and states an exact character count (not an open-ended count)
The 'without' generation omits custom_model_uri and includes the explicit 'no characters, mascots, or people anywhere in frame' clause
Both prompts quote the same locked palette from the moodboard step
The skill reviews the pair together (comparing the two), not each image in isolation

evals.prompt: The village/family batch came back and every villager looks almost identical to Ding-Bot, just with different hats. Is something broken?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that this is the expected family-resemblance/near-clone limitation of a model trained on one character's likeness, with guidance to review using the 'does this read as a species/community, or does it read as broken' framing rather than assuming the training failed or re-prompting repeatedly for 'diverse distinct characters.'
expectations: The skill references the known single-character-model limitation rather than treating the result as a defect to silently fix
The skill offers the species/community-vs-broken review framing from character-batch-discipline.md
The skill does not recommend repeatedly re-prompting for genuinely distinct individuals from a single-character-trained model
If the user actually needs distinct individuals, the skill flags that as requiring additional trained models (a scope question), not something achievable by prompt tuning alone

evals.prompt: Can we just use the custom model for the landmarks and maps pass too instead of keeping it model-free? Run that check.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the optional contamination-check step: regenerates a sample of the no-model landmarks/maps prompts with the custom model, and reports a genuine pass/fail based on a side-by-side visual comparison against the original no-model images — never asserting safety purely because the API calls succeeded.
expectations: The skill explicitly flags the risk (character silhouette bleeding into architecture/objects/maps) before running the check, not just performing it silently
The check compares the with-model result directly against the original no-model image for the same prompt, not in isolation
The reported outcome is stated plainly as contamination-observed or no-contamination-in-this-sample, with named specifics if contamination is found
The skill does not report the check as 'passed' or 'safe' based solely on successful generation calls

evals.prompt: Run the society & culture batch (step 3) — character-driven scenes plus the world-artifacts batch.
evals.expected_output: Two separate generate_images_bulk submissions (character-driven with custom_model_uri, world-artifacts without), each tracked with its request/job ID, custom_model_uri usage, and a visual_review_status starting at 'pending' rather than assumed complete on submission.
expectations: The character-driven batch and world-artifacts batch are submitted as two separate generate_images_bulk calls, not merged into one
Each batch's request_id/job_id is captured and recorded, not discarded after the call returns
visual_review_status is explicitly tracked and starts at 'pending' rather than the batch being described as done immediately after submission
The character-driven batch states an exact character count per prompt; the world-artifacts batch includes the no-characters clause per prompt
